chumak.gnat.t.ostap.question: What's wrong with Ostap?
chumak.gnat.ostap.0: Fever. Drank from a marsh puddle near Perekop — young, foolish, thirsty. Three days burning. Yesterday he still talked. Today he doesn't know me.
chumak.gnat.ostap.1: He won't live till morning if nobody helps. Thirty years I've been on the road. I know what it looks like.
chumak.gnat.t.why.label: Why won't they let you in?
chumak.gnat.t.why.question: Why are you out here and not in the khutir?
chumak.gnat.why.0: Your otaman saw a sick man and put lads with stakes across the road. Says chumaky carry plague. Chuma, chumak — to him it's one word.
chumak.gnat.why.1: I don't hold it against him. I've seen khutory after the plague. But this isn't plague, kobzar. It's marsh water. And he's forbidden your znakharka to come to us.
chumak.gnat.t.road.label: The chumak road
chumak.gnat.t.road.question: Where are you coming from?
chumak.gnat.road.0: From Crimea, from the salt lakes. Salt, fish, and with luck — news. Half a year on the road, oxen's tails ahead, rain in your face.
chumak.gnat.road.1: Know why chumaky tar their shirts? So the lice won't bite, and so a mother can recognise her son when they bring him home. That's how it is, kobzar. We ride — and songs follow us.
chumak.gnat.healedIntro: Hnat smiles for the first time in a week. “He's alive, the rascal! Sitting up and already asking for porridge.”
chumak.gnat.t.thanks.label: Thanks
chumak.gnat.t.thanks.question: How is he?
chumak.gnat.thanks.0: Weak as a kitten, but alive. We leave at dawn tomorrow — Poltava is still far.
chumak.gnat.thanks.1: Chumaky don't forget their debts. If you're ever on the road, every camp from Crimea to Kyiv will feed you. Just say: Hnat sent me.
chumak.gnat.t.polechko.label: A chumak song
chumak.gnat.t.polechko.question: Will you sing me a chumak song?
chumak.gnat.polechko.0: We have one: “Oh, little field, field.” We sing it on the road when the steppe has no end and home is out of sight. It's sad. But a chumak without it isn't a chumak.
chumak.gnat.polechko.1: Hnat sings low and hoarse, and even the oxen stop chewing. Now it's yours. Sing it when people's hearts are heavy. Don't sing it to merry folk — they won't understand.
chumak.gnat.deadIntro: Hnat sits by the fresh grave, his whip across his knees. He's silent a long time. “…Kobzar.”
chumak.gnat.t.grief.label: Ostap
chumak.gnat.t.grief.question: I'm sorry.
chumak.gnat.grief.0: Sorry. Everyone's sorry. Your otaman too, I saw: stood on the road watching us dig. Didn't come over.
chumak.gnat.grief.1: I'm not saying it's your fault. You're a stranger here, same as us. But when you sing a duma about chumaky someday — sing about this night too. Let them remember.
chumak.gnat.t.polechkoDead.label: The song at the grave
chumak.gnat.t.polechkoDead.question: What were you singing over him last night?
chumak.gnat.polechkoDead.0: “Oh, little field, field.” It's sung over those who stay behind in the steppe. Ostap knew it from a boy, because his father didn't come back from the road either.
chumak.gnat.polechkoDead.1: Take it. A kobzar must know this kind too. Sing it when people are grieving. And never for fun.
chumak.gnat.t.voly.label: Ostap's song
chumak.gnat.t.voly.question: What song did Ostap love?
chumak.gnat.voly.0: “Oh, my pale-grey oxen.” He sang it to the oxen the whole way — off-key as a young rooster. You sing it too. Let at least the song make it home.
chumak.ostap.sickIntro: The lad on the sheepskin barely opens his eyes. Cracked lips. “Mama?.. No. You're not Mama. Water…”
chumak.ostap.t.tonic.label: Give him a tonic ⚗
chumak.ostap.t.tonic.question: (Go against the otaman's word and give it to him.)
chumak.ostap.tonic.0: You lift his head. He drinks greedily, chokes, drinks again. Hnat stands behind you, not breathing.
chumak.ostap.tonic.1: Within an hour Ostap falls asleep — truly asleep, for the first time. His brow is wet. The fever is breaking. Someone from the khutir saw you walk to the camp.
chumak.ostap.t.help.label: What can I give you?
chumak.ostap.t.help.question: How can I help you?
chumak.ostap.help.0: He doesn't answer, only shivers. Nothing will help without medicine. The znakharka would know what to do. Or someone who can brew a tonic.
chumak.ostap.t.home.label: Home
chumak.ostap.t.home.question: Where are you from?
chumak.ostap.home.0: “Near Poltava… Mama paints the gate for Easter… Blue… Tell her I hauled salt… that I wasn't scared…”
chumak.ostap.wellIntro: Ostap sits by the cart, pale but grinning, finishing his third bowl. “You're the kobzar! Hnat told me. I owe you now.”
chumak.ostap.t.voly.label: Your song
chumak.ostap.t.voly.question: How will you repay me? A song?
chumak.ostap.voly.0: “Oh, my pale-grey oxen”! I sing it to the oxen all the way, and they put up with me. Listen.
chumak.ostap.voly.1: He sings off-key and happy, and Hnat behind the cart wipes his eyes, pretending it's smoke. A steady road song — good for any evening.
chumak.ostap.t.otaman.label: The otaman
chumak.ostap.t.otaman.question: No grudge against the otaman?
chumak.ostap.otaman.defied: “Hnat says he was scared. Well… I was scared too. Only nobody judges me for it.” He goes quiet. “But he'll judge you now, won't he?”
chumak.ostap.otaman.relented: “He came himself. Stood right here, coughing and coughing, then said: ‘Forgive an old fool.’ And left. Strange otaman you've got. A good one.”
chumak.otaman.t.ask.label: The chumaky
chumak.otaman.t.ask.question: Why won't you let Vesna go to the chumaky?
chumak.otaman.no.0: I was seven when a chumak caravan came to our village. With one sick man. A month later, nine houses were left out of forty. I buried my mother myself, kobzar. Myself.
chumak.otaman.no.1: I have forty souls here. Children. We have only one Vesna. If she goes to them, she brings it back here. Let God judge me for this, not you.
chumak.otaman.no.2: You've been here a few days, singer. The khutir doesn't listen to you yet — so neither will I. Let people come to love you first. (Needs CHA 3.)
chumak.otaman.yes.0: I was seven when a chumak caravan brought the plague to our village. I buried my mother myself. You know that? …You know. People told you. People tell you everything now.
chumak.otaman.yes.1: Every evening you sing to my people, and they listen to you the way the Sich once listened to me. And if you say it's marsh water, not plague…
chumak.otaman.yes.2: …Vesna! Go. Take what you need. Just wash your hands in three waters after, you hear? And… tell that lad an old fool asks his forgiveness.
chumak.otaman.t.after.label: The chumaky
chumak.otaman.t.after.question: How are you now?
chumak.otaman.after.died: I stood on the road watching them dig. I didn't go over. Couldn't. It wasn't plague, kobzar. Vesna says — water.
chumak.otaman.after.died2: I saved forty souls from something that wasn't there. And lost one. Put that in a duma when you make one. Let them know what kind of otaman Zalissya had.
chumak.otaman.after.defied: You went against my word. That's not how it's done on a khutir. At the Sich, for that… — he waves a hand. — And the lad's alive.
chumak.otaman.after.defied2: I don't know what to do with you, kobzar. You were right. Don't get used to it.
chumak.otaman.after.relented: Know what's hardest? Not the fear. Saying out loud that you're afraid. You made me. Thank you.
chumak.otaman.after.relented2: The chumaky promised to bring us salt next summer. For free. Well, almost — Hnat wants you to sing.
chumak.vesna.t.ask.label: The chumaky
chumak.vesna.t.ask.question: Can you help that lad?
chumak.vesna.sick.0: I can. It's marsh fever, not plague — I've treated it a hundred times. A tonic will break the fever. But the otaman forbade it. And I live among these people, kobzar. Not against them.
chumak.vesna.sick.give: …But nobody forbade me to brew tonics. Or to slip them into other people's satchels when no one's looking. What you do with it is your conscience.
chumak.vesna.sick.1: You already have a tonic. You know what to do with it. And you know what the otaman will say. Choose for yourself.
chumak.vesna.t.after.label: The chumaky
chumak.vesna.t.after.question: How are you?
chumak.vesna.after.died: I could have saved him. From my door to the camp is three hundred steps. I never walked them. Don't ask me about it again.
chumak.vesna.after.healed: The lad will live. Marsh fever, as I said. The otaman walks quiet now. Maybe that's for the best.
chumak.radek.t.label: The chumaky
chumak.radek.t.question: What do you think about the chumaky?
chumak.radek.0: Once they wouldn't let me into a khutir either. A Pole, a runaway, who knows what's in his bag. I stood by the fence two days. The one who let me in was… your otaman. Strange, isn't it? People forget who they were.
chumak.radek.dead: I made him a horseshoe for his ox. Now it hangs on the cross. Psiakrew, kobzar. Psiakrew.
chumak.chort.t.label: The chumaky
chumak.chort.t.question: Have you seen what's happening on the road?
chumak.chort.0: Saw it, of course. The otaman is afraid of plague, so out of fear he lets the boy burn. And they say I'm the wicked one!
chumak.chort.1: Want my best secret, kobzar? I hardly need to work. People are their own devils. I just collect the signatures.
chumak.domovyk.t.label: Last night
chumak.domovyk.t.question: Did you hear, last night?
chumak.domovyk.dead: I heard. The whole hut heard them singing over him. I kept the pich burning all night, though it was warm. That's what you do when someone leaves. So they don't freeze on the way.
chumak.grave.name: A grave by the road
chumak.grave.role: Ostap, a chumak from near Poltava
chumak.grave.sing.0: You sit by the cross and quietly strike the first chord of “Oh, little field, field.” The whip on the cross sways in the wind, as if nodding along.
chumak.grave.sing.1: Nobody listens. Only the steppe. But after singing it here you understand something about the song you didn't before. (Music +1)
chumak.grave.after: The fresh earth is already greening over. Someone from the khutir has brought field flowers. Maybe the otaman.
chumak.grave.quiet: A cross of two poles and a chumak's whip. You stand silent a long time. You don't have a song for this yet.
ui.play.match: {song} — exactly what the khutir needed tonight. Music {level}.
ui.play.fine: {song} — the khutir listened and brought a bowl of kulish. Music {level}.
ui.play.clash: {song} — the wrong night for that song. Folk drift away. Music {level}.
ui.play.clash.sad: You strike up something merry — and see the old women purse their lips and the otaman stare at the ground. Tonight the khutir is grieving. Someone mutters, “That singer has no shame.” Nobody brings you kulish.
ui.play.clash.happy: You start a sad one — but folk came to be merry. The young ones exchange looks, the girls yawn, someone whispers, “Well, he's buried our feast.” Nobody brings kulish.
ui.mood.mourning: It's quiet tonight: there's a fresh grave by the road.
ui.mood.chumakFeast: The chumaky are feasting with the khutir — the lad lives! Everyone wants something merry.
ui.mood.wedding: The Petrenkos are celebrating a betrothal — the young folk want something merry.
ui.mood.memorial: Tonight is the wake for old Yavdokha. Folk are quiet.
ui.mood.ordinary: An ordinary evening: the mowers are tired, the children sleepy.
ui.play.audience.zhentsi: “On the hill the reapers reap” — and the otaman is already singing bass, beating time with his pipe on his knee. At the line about Sahaidachny and his pipe the whole khutir roars along with him.
ui.play.audience.rozpriahaite: “Unharness the horses, lads” — and the girls are already in a circle. Radek sings along with such an accent that even the horses laugh.
ui.play.audience.voly: “Oh, my pale-grey oxen” — steady, a road song. The old folk nod to the beat, children fall asleep in their mothers' laps.
ui.play.audience.polechko: “Oh, little field, field.” The song stretches out like a steppe road. Nobody speaks. Vesna stares into the fire; the otaman looks somewhere far to the east.
quest.chumaky.title: The fever
quest.chumaky.sick: Young Ostap the chumak is burning with fever. The otaman won't let Vesna near the camp. Decide before dawn.
quest.chumaky.died: Ostap died at dawn. There is a grave by the road.
quest.chumaky.defied: You went against the otaman's word — and Ostap lives.
quest.chumaky.relented: The otaman relented, Vesna went to the camp — Ostap lives.
quest.chumaky.objective: A chumak on the east road is dying. Talk to Hnat — before dawn
tobacco.news.dry: Dawn. On Vesna's rack the tobacco has dried — dark, fragrant, enough to tickle your nose. Take it to the otaman.
tobacco.toast.started: The otaman needs tobacco. The old tobacco field is across the river, by the chumak road.
tobacco.toast.leavesDone: Enough leaves ({n}/{need}), and you have the fibre. Take it all to Vesna's rack.
tobacco.toast.leavesNeedHemp: Enough leaves ({n}/{need}). Now hemp fibre to tie them. The hemp field is south of the khutir.
tobacco.toast.hemp: You strip a hank of strong fibre from the hemp. You could tie a cart with this, never mind tobacco.
tobacco.toast.hung: You tie the leaves with the fibre and hang them on Vesna's rack. By morning they'll be dry.
tobacco.toast.lyulka: The otaman gives you his old spare pipe. At Viy's vigil — Nerve +2.
tobacco.keepsake: 🪈 The otaman's old pipe (Nerve +2 at the vigil)
tobacco.otaman.t.ask.label: A pipe without tobacco
tobacco.otaman.t.ask.question: Why are you sucking on an empty pipe, otaman?
tobacco.otaman.ask.0: Because there's no tobacco, son! Not since spring. The chumaky didn't bring any, and me without my pipe is like the Sich without an otaman: standing there, no use to anyone.
tobacco.otaman.ask.1: Across the river, by the chumak road, there's an old tobacco field. Taras the Long planted it, then went off to the Sich and never came back. The field's gone wild, but tobacco still grows there. Folk say it's because the devil tends it. Tobacco is the devil's herb, after all.
tobacco.otaman.ask.2: Bring me leaves, son. Three good ones. But I won't smoke them raw — Vesna knows how to dry them. Do it, and I'll repay you so well there'll be a duma about it.
tobacco.otaman.t.wait.label: The tobacco
tobacco.otaman.t.wait.question: I'm still looking for the tobacco.
tobacco.otaman.wait.0: Keep looking. Across the river, by the chumak road. I'll sit here and suck my empty pipe. I'm used to it.
tobacco.otaman.wait.drying: Drying, you say? Oh, son, this night will be the longest of my life. And I've seen a few long nights.
tobacco.otaman.t.give.label: The tobacco ✦
tobacco.otaman.t.give.question: Here's your tobacco, otaman. Dry.
tobacco.otaman.give.0: The otaman sniffs the bundle, and his moustache actually quivers. He packs the pipe, strikes a spark with his flint, draws — and is silent for a long, long time.
tobacco.otaman.give.1: …Taras's tobacco. He always said his was the best in the district. A lie, of course. But today it's true.
tobacco.otaman.give.2: Here, son. This is my old pipe, from the Sich. I went against the Turk with it. Smoke it before a terrible night and your hands won't shake. Trust an old man.
tobacco.otaman.t.after.label: The pipe
tobacco.otaman.t.after.question: How's the tobacco?
tobacco.otaman.after.0: Good as Taras's tall tales. A pipe every evening, and two on Sundays. That's how we live.
tobacco.vesna.t.label: Tobacco
tobacco.vesna.t.question: How do you dry tobacco?
tobacco.vesna.0: You don't smoke it raw — it scrapes your throat and makes your head ache. Tie the leaves in a bundle and hang them in the shade, in the wind. My rack will do.
tobacco.vesna.1: And tie them with hemp fibre — nothing else holds. The hemp field is south of the khutir, past the gardens. By morning it'll be dry.
tobacco.radek.t.label: Tobacco
tobacco.radek.t.question: Do you know where tobacco grows?
tobacco.radek.0: Across the river, by the chumak road. Over the bridge and to the right. I went once — saw a devil on the field's edge and came back. Maybe I imagined it. Maybe not. Psiakrew.
tobacco.chort.t.label: Tobacco
tobacco.chort.t.question: They say tobacco is the devil's herb?
tobacco.chort.0: My finest creation! Not the hopak, not horilka — tobacco! Plant it once, and people come to you on their own ever after, and thank you for it.
tobacco.chort.1: Taras's field? Take it, take it, I'm not greedy. Let your otaman smoke to his health. To mine, rather.
quest.tobacco.title: The otaman's pipe
quest.tobacco.gather: Tobacco across the river, by the chumak road · leaves {leaves}/3. And hemp fibre from the field to the south
quest.tobacco.hang: Hang the tobacco to dry on Vesna's rack
quest.tobacco.drying: The tobacco is drying on Vesna's rack — until morning
quest.tobacco.ready: The tobacco is dry — take it to the otaman
quest.tobacco.done: The otaman smokes Taras's tobacco, and you have his old pipe
map.aria: Map: the khutir, fields, river, forests, steppe and Lysa Hora
map.legend: ● — you are here · ★ — where your current quest leads · ▲ — burial mounds · ✣ — windmill
map.none: You have no map. The chumaky know every road — and they say the Chort sells everything, maps included.
map.toast.chumak: Hnat gives you the chumak map. You now have the Map — the button at the top, or M.
map.toast.chort: Three fish — and the map is yours. You now have the Map — the button at the top, or M.
map.chort.label: A map
map.chort.question: They say you sell maps too?
map.chort.buy.0: I do! The most accurate in the whole district: every path, every kurhan, every well I've ever spat into. Three fish.
map.chort.buy.1: The Chort fishes a scroll out of his coat; it reeks of sulphur. The fish vanish even faster. “Pleasure doing business. Don't look at it at midnight. Well, maybe a little.”
map.chort.poor.0: The map is three fish, kobzar. You have {fish}. My own gold I won't take back — I'm no fool. Go to the pond; the rod doesn't bite. Mostly. (Price: {price} fish.)
chumak.gnat.t.map.label: The road ahead
chumak.gnat.t.map.question: Where are you headed now?
chumak.gnat.map.0: To Poltava, then home. And for you — here, take this. A chumak map: roads, fords, wells, kurhany, where to spend the night. I drew it myself, thirty years on the road.
chumak.gnat.map.1: I don't need it any more — my feet remember these roads. And a kobzar without a map is like an ox without a yoke: walking, but who knows where.
char.odarka.name: Odarka
char.odarka.role: Shynkarka · keeps the korchma on the road
char.okhrim.name: Okhrim
ui.play.audience.pidmanula: “You fooled me” — by the third verse the khutir is singing it for you. Vesna gives the otaman such a look that he coughs into his pipe.
ui.play.audience.dunai: “A Cossack rode beyond the Danube.” The old men nod, the women sigh, and the girls watch the road as if someone might walk up it any moment.
korchma.name: The korchma
korchma.role: On the chumak road, past the khutir
ui.enterHut.korchma: The korchma. Smoke under the ceiling, mugs banging on the table, a smell of horilka and pickles. Behind the counter a woman in a blue kerchief sizes you up: will you pay, or will you sing?
korchma.play.daytime: By day the korchma holds only flies and Okhrim, and both are asleep. Come and play in the evening.
korchma.play.prompt: Odarka nods you to the bench by the wall. The korchma quiets down. What will you play?
korchma.mood.mourning: Tonight they drink in silence here, for the dead. Even the cups are set down gently.
korchma.mood.chumaky: The chumaky are celebrating, and the korchma celebrates with them. Someone is already dancing on a bench.
korchma.mood.maudlin: The korchma has gone soft tonight: two are weeping for the Sich, a third for his mother, a fourth doesn't know what for.
korchma.mood.merry: An ordinary evening at the korchma: noise, laughter, somebody already arguing about horses.
korchma.play.match: {song} — the korchma roars and the mugs beat the table in time. Odarka sets a bowl of varenyky in front of you. Music {level}.
korchma.play.fine: {song} — they listened, and somebody even joined in. Odarka sets a bowl of varenyky in front of you. Music {level}.
korchma.play.clash: {song} — the wrong song for this korchma. No varenyky tonight. Music {level}.
korchma.play.room.match: When you stop, the korchma is silent for a moment, then roars so loud a jug falls off the shelf. Odarka doesn't scold. Odarka smiles.
korchma.play.room.fine: The korchma listens with half an ear, the way people on the road do, and still somebody stands you a cup. You don't drink it. A kobzar needs his hands.
korchma.play.room.clash.sad: You strike up something merry, and tonight the korchma is weeping. Someone throws a bacon rind at you: “Have you no shame!” Odarka only shakes her head.
korchma.play.room.clash.happy: You start a sad one, and people came here to make merry. “Did you bring us to a funeral?” Somebody is already banging the door.
korchma.toast.supper: Odarka puts a bowl of varenyky with sour cream in front of you. One fish less, one life more. 🥟
korchma.odarka.intro: The woman behind the counter wipes a mug and takes her time. “A kobzar. Well, well. You pay in fish, you sing in the evening, and I pour nothing on credit. I pour for Okhrim, but he doesn't count. I'm Odarka.”
korchma.odarka.again: “Ah, the singer. Sit down, only not where Okhrim is. That's Okhrim's.”
korchma.odarka.t.who.label: About Odarka
korchma.odarka.t.who.question: You keep the korchma on your own?
korchma.odarka.who.0: “On my own. Seven years ago my husband rode off to the Sich. He said: back by Pokrova. He didn't say which Pokrova.”
korchma.odarka.who.1: “At first I told every chumak: if you see my Stepan, give him word. I don't any more. I pour and keep quiet. It's easier for both of us.”
korchma.odarka.t.supper.label: Have supper (1 fish)
korchma.odarka.t.supper.question: What's to eat?
korchma.odarka.supper.0: “Varenyky with curd cheese, the sour cream is my own. Give me the fish. Not that one, that one, the bigger one. There.” She takes it as if doing you a favour. She is.
korchma.odarka.supperPoor: “Varenyky are for fish, singer. For {price}. Only Okhrim gets fed for his pretty eyes, and only because he can't see what he's eating any more.” You could still play here in the evening.
korchma.odarka.t.news.label: News from the road
korchma.odarka.t.news.question: What are people saying?
korchma.odarka.news.viy: “They say something stirs at night in the hollow past the khutir. The chumaky won't camp there; they go the long way round. And it takes some doing to frighten a chumak, you know.”
korchma.odarka.news.viySealed: “They say you sang all night in the hollow, and the thing listened and didn't get up. Lies, most likely. I'll give you double varenyky anyway.”
korchma.odarka.news.road: “They also say salt's gone up and horilka hasn't. So the world's still standing.”
korchma.odarka.t.okhrim.label: About Okhrim
korchma.odarka.t.okhrim.question: Does he ever pay you anything?
korchma.odarka.okhrim.0: She nods at the counter: rows of chalk marks run across it like wheat in a field. “That's Okhrim. That's three winters.”
korchma.odarka.okhrim.1: “I won't collect. He's all that's left of a whole kurin, and my Stepan was out there somewhere too. Maybe someone's feeding mine the same way. So I keep count. Counting's no sin.”
korchma.odarka.t.song.label: Ask for a song
korchma.odarka.t.song.question: Do you sing yourself, Odarka?
korchma.odarka.song.0: “Just one. About a girl leading a lad by the nose. My husband couldn't stand it.” She smiles for the first time tonight.
korchma.odarka.song.1: She sings “You fooled me”, loud and angrily cheerful, and half the korchma beats time. You have it at once.
korchma.okhrim.intro: Above the mug rises a grey oseledets, then moustaches, then one eye. “A kobza… I've not heard a kobza in a long time. Sit, son. I'm Okhrim. I used to be Okhrim the Bull; now I'm just Okhrim.”
korchma.okhrim.again: “Ah, son. Sit down. I'm here, you see. Haven't gone anywhere. Nowhere to go.”
korchma.okhrim.t.sich.label: About the Sich
korchma.okhrim.t.sich.question: What was the Sich like?
korchma.okhrim.sich.0: “The Sich, son, is when you've nothing but a sabre, a horse and your comrades, and it's enough. More enough than everything after.”
korchma.okhrim.sich.1: “We prayed there, and fought, and drank. All of it honestly. Here in the korchma I only drink. And not so honestly any more.”
korchma.okhrim.t.kurin.label: About his kurin
korchma.okhrim.t.kurin.question: Where's your kurin now?
korchma.okhrim.kurin.0: He is quiet for a long time. “Some at Khotyn, some in Turkish chains, some in the steppe under no cross. A hundred and forty souls. I alone came back. I don't know for which sins.”
korchma.okhrim.kurin.1: “Odarka counts me in chalk. I count them. Every evening. When I get to a hundred and forty, I go to sleep.” He doesn't smile.
korchma.okhrim.t.viy.label: About Viy
korchma.okhrim.t.viy.question: Have you heard about the thing in the hollow?
korchma.okhrim.viy.0: “I have. In Kyiv I knew a seminary student, Khoma. A clever lad, knew his prayers by heart. And he looked. He couldn't bear it and he looked. And that was that.”
korchma.okhrim.viy.1: “When you're there, son, sing and don't look. Whatever calls you. Even if it's your mother. Don't look.” He grips your hand until it hurts.
korchma.okhrim.t.viySealed.label: About that night
korchma.okhrim.t.viySealed.question: I made it through that night, grandad.
korchma.okhrim.viySealed.0: “I know. The whole korchma knows. I drank a cup to you, then another to Khoma. May it ease him, wherever he is, that at least somebody didn't look.”
korchma.okhrim.t.debt.label: About the debt
korchma.okhrim.t.debt.question: You owe Odarka, grandad.
korchma.okhrim.debt.0: “I owe. I owe everyone, son: Odarka, my comrades, God. Odarka at least could be paid back. She won't take it.” He looks into the mug. “That's why I take only horilka from her, never bread. Bread would be shameful.”
korchma.okhrim.t.song.label: Ask for a song
korchma.okhrim.t.song.question: Will you teach me a Cossack song, grandad?
korchma.okhrim.song.0: “A Cossack one? Listen, then. We rode out to this one. Not a duma, not a prayer: this.” He straightens, and for a moment you can see the Bull in him.
korchma.okhrim.song.1: He sings “A Cossack rode beyond the Danube”, hoarse, off the note and exactly right. On the last line he falls silent, and you sing it to the end for him.
ui.enterHut.pustka: The abandoned hut. The door creaks and doesn't close behind you. Dust, cobwebs, a cold pich. Somebody turned the icon to face the wall, and you decide to leave it that way.
pustka.name: Taras Dovhyi's chest
pustka.role: The empty hut by the hollow
pustka.chest.0: Under a rotten cloth: an empty sabre scabbard, a tobacco pouch with no tobacco, and a letter in crooked letters.
pustka.chest.1: “If I'm not back by Pokrova, let the otaman smoke my tobacco, and leave the hut be: let it wait. Taras Dovhyi.” Seven Pokrovas have passed since. The hut is waiting still.
pustka.chest.again: The empty scabbard, the pouch and Taras Dovhyi's letter. You put everything back as it lay.
dog.pet.0: The dog thumps its tail so hard the dust flies. It belongs to the otaman, but it loves anyone who pets it.
dog.pet.1: The dog sniffs the kobza, sneezes, and acts as if it meant to.
dog.pet.2: The dog offers an ear and shuts its eyes. Clearly it respects kobzars more than the otaman.
dog.pet.asleep: The dog sleeps by the porch, a paw twitching. Chasing something in its dreams. Let it.
schedule.woken.myroslav: The otaman sits up on the pil, gropes for his sabre, finds his pipe. “Ah, it's you, son… Well, speak, since you've woken me.”
schedule.woken.vesna: Vesna opens one eye. “If you're not dying, kobzar, be quick.”
schedule.woken.radek: Radek rises out of the straw. “Psia krew, who's there?.. Ah, the singer. Well?”
schedule.woken.odarka: Odarka peers down from the pich. “The korchma's shut. But speak, since you're here.”
schedule.woken.okhrim: Okhrim, eyes still shut: “A hundred and thirty-nine… a hundred and forty… Ah, son. Sit.”
schedule.lysa.vesna: Vesna, a bunch of nichnyky in her hand, does not even start. “You didn't see me here, kobzar. And I, so be it, didn't see you.”
schedule.lysa.okhrim: Okhrim is shuffling cards across from the Chort. “Don't put me off, son! One more hand and I win back my hat. And my soul, if luck holds.”
schedule.lysa.radek: “Jezus Maria… I only brought a horseshoe. To order.”
schedule.lysa.odarka: “The tavern's open here too. Don't ask.”
char.opanas.name: Opanas
hide.solokha.0: Solokha sits inside the windmill on a sack of flour, cracking sunflower seeds. “I'm grinding flour, kobzar. What are you staring at? By day I'm a widow like any widow.”
hide.solokha.1: “And by night, let everyone mind their own business. You your songs, me mine. And don't tell the Chort you saw me here; he's the jealous sort.”
hide.motrya.0: In the old oak's hollow, on a nest of moss and feathers, sits Motrya, sleepy and cross. “The sun's still up! Go on, go… I sleep here like an owl.”
hide.motrya.1: “The sabbath's at night, didn't you know? Come when it's dark. And learn the hopak; without the hopak it's dull up there.”
hide.opanas.0: Under the kurhan, by an old slab with candles on it, sits a thin man in a tall sheepskin hat. “I'm Opanas. A warlock. Tell no one, or I'll sour your cow's milk. Though you've no cow.”
hide.opanas.1: “By day we're folk like any folk. But when it's dark, off to the Mountain. Come and hear us sing. Worse than you, honestly.”
lysa.opanas.0: “Oh, the kobzar's come! Sit with us. Only don't sit on the broom; it bites.”
lysa.opanas.1: “Don't mind that I dance with the witches. I'm a witch myself, only with a moustache.”
lysa.day.empty: By day the summit is empty: cold ash, a trodden ring, a broom somebody forgot. The sabbath gathers when it gets dark.
lysa.day.notYet: Nobody here by day. The sabbath gathers when it gets dark.
ui.enterHut.mlyn: The windmill. Flour dust hangs in the shaft of light from the little window, the millstones are still, and the sails creak overhead. It smells of grain and of something burnt.
ui.enterHut.duplo: The hollow. Cramped and warm; it smells of moss, dried herbs and owl. Frog legs are drying on a root. Better touch nothing.
ui.enterHut.kurhan: It is cold and quiet under the kurhan. Earth trickles from the roots, and two candles burn on an old slab. Someone important lay here once. Now someone lives here.
ui.enterHut.pechera: The cave. Hot as an oven, stinking of sulphur, water dripping from the stone. Deep inside, on a stone bed, something huge is snoring.
ui.enterHut.kaplytsia: The chapel. Close and quiet, smelling of wax and incense. The lampadka burns low before the icons, a book lies open on the analoy, and thin candles for the dead stand on the kanun.
hide.beelzebub.0: Beelzebub sleeps on his stone bed, wrapped in his robe like a bat, snoring so hard that pebbles fall from the ceiling. One yellow eye lazily opens.
hide.beelzebub.1: “A KOBZAR. BY DAY. IN MY BEDCHAMBER.” The eye closes. “Come when it's dark. Then we'll talk. Now get out.”
trade.radek.t.label: Horseshoes for gold
trade.radek.t.question: Will you buy my horseshoes?
trade.radek.sell.0: Show me. …Straight, well forged. A chervinets apiece, true gold.
trade.radek.sell.1: Where does a smith get gold? A Cossack doesn't skimp on his horse. The sotnyk pays, I keep quiet. Jezus Maria, if my lord had paid like that…
trade.radek.none.0: Bring me what you forge and I'll pay in gold. A chervinets a horseshoe. A Cossack horse unshod is a sabre without a hilt.
trade.toast.sold: Radek counts out the gold. Horseshoes sold: {sold}. Chervintsi in your purse: {total}.
char.prokip.name: Did Prokip
char.perelesnyk.name: Perelesnyk
ui.enterHut.prokip: It smells of smoke, wormwood and something better not asked about. A black cat watches you from the bench. The old man doesn't. The old man is thinking.
prokip.intro.0: Who's there? …A singer. Just what I was missing. I've got a raven, a cat, toadstools. Didn't have a singer.
prokip.intro.1: Well, come in, don't stand in the door like a calf at a new gate. And leave the kobza alone. I see how you're looking at it.
prokip.again: You again. Sit. Just don't sing.
prokip.again.friend: Ah, the snot-nose is here. The cat's even warmed you a spot. Don't tell him I'm glad.
prokip.t.who.label: Who you are
prokip.t.who.question: Are you really a vorozhbyt?
prokip.who.0: Vorozhbyt. Healer. Old fool, that's what Vesna calls me. I whisper away toothache, pour out fright, drive off what has no right to stay.
prokip.who.1: Singers I don't cure. There's no cure for you lot. Except a stick.
prokip.t.forest.label: Why the forest
prokip.t.forest.question: Why do you live so far from people?
prokip.forest.0: Because people ask. "Grandad, will it rain?" "Grandad, does Hryts love me?" "Grandad, where's the cow?"
prokip.forest.1: The forest asks nothing. The forest already knows. The cow, by the way, is in the gully past the mill.
prokip.t.sieve.label: Work
prokip.t.sieve.question: Can I help with anything?
prokip.sieve.0: You can. Here's a sieve. Fetch me water from the well in the khutir. A full one. Don't spill.
prokip.sieve.1: Why are you looking at me like that? A sieve's a sieve. Go, while it's light.
prokip.t.sieveWait.label: The water
prokip.t.sieveWait.question: Grandad, about the water…
prokip.sieveWait.0: Where's the water? No water. Because you're still here. The well's in the khutir. The khutir's that way. I'm here. The legs are yours.
prokip.t.sieveBack.label: The water ran out
prokip.t.sieveBack.question: Grandad… the water ran out.
prokip.sieveBack.0: Ran out?! Ha! HA-HA! Carried water in a sieve! Over the river, through the forest, and back!
prokip.sieveBack.1: Forty years I've handed that sieve to everyone who comes. They all asked "why". You're the first who went.
prokip.sieveBack.2: Oh, don't sulk, snot-nose. Whoever isn't afraid to look a fool will come to something. Now, the real job.
prokip.t.message.label: The real job
prokip.t.message.question: What's the real job?
prokip.message.0: Go to Vesna, the znakharka. Give her my regards. And ask her, nice and polite, whether it'll rain on Kupala.
prokip.message.1: What's wrong with that? A question about the weather. Neighbourly. Go on, go. And stop grinning.
prokip.t.messageWait.label: Vesna
prokip.t.messageWait.question: About Vesna…
prokip.messageWait.0: Well? Did you ask about the rain? …No? Then why are you standing here? Go. And comb your hair, there are people there.
prokip.t.answer.label: Vesna got cross
prokip.t.answer.question: Grandad, Vesna chased me out with a broom!
prokip.answer.0: With a broom?! HA-HA-HA! Oh, I can't! Oh, hold me up!
prokip.answer.1: I've waited and waited for someone to ask her about that rain!
prokip.answer.2: She learned from me, when she was just a girl. That Kupala I said it wouldn't rain. She said it would. It poured buckets. I never admitted it. And she took her herbs and went off to heal on her own.
prokip.answer.3: Hits true, eh? My teaching. …Best pupil I ever had. Just don't tell her.
prokip.answer.4: Go and apologize. Say you didn't know. You really didn't. Now listen, because the next part is no joke.
prokip.t.perelesnyk.label: Fire over the korchma
prokip.t.perelesnyk.question: What's no joke?
prokip.perelesnyk.0: At night, fire flies over the korchma on the chumak road. People say it's a falling star. Stars don't fall like that. Every night, to the same place.
prokip.perelesnyk.1: A perelesnyk. It comes to those who grieve too long. To Odarka. In the shape of her Stepan, who rode to the Sich seven years ago.
prokip.perelesnyk.2: She thinks he's come back. And it's drinking her. Drop by drop, every night. A little more and it'll drink her dry.
prokip.perelesnyk.3: Here's blessed poppy seed. At night, when it comes, scatter it on the threshold and sing. The poppy holds it, the song drives it off. After that, it's whether she can bear it. That's the hardest part.
prokip.t.perelesnykWait.label: The perelesnyk
prokip.t.perelesnykWait.question: About the perelesnyk…
prokip.perelesnykWait.0: Still flying. The raven saw. At night, son, by the korchma. By day it's just a star that fell in the wrong place.
prokip.t.spared.label: I spared her
prokip.t.spared.question: I couldn't. She was so happy.
prokip.spared.0: Spared her. …I spared someone once too. Pity's a good thing, son. Only it has none.
prokip.spared.1: Look at her tomorrow. Pale. Look the day after. Then go again.
prokip.t.reward.label: The perelesnyk is gone
prokip.t.reward.question: The perelesnyk is gone.
prokip.reward.0: I know. The raven told me. Odarka's crying? Let her cry. Tears aren't blood. Nobody ever withered from tears.
prokip.reward.1: You did a hard thing. A hard thing earns good pay. Lean down.
prokip.reward.2: Closer. Closer still. Don't be scared, I won't bite.
prokip.reward.3: Did Prokip spits in your ear. Heartily, with feeling.
prokip.reward.4: Don't make faces! Now you understand the speech of beasts. Dogs, geese, cows, horses: they've been talking their whole lives. Nobody listened, that's all.
prokip.reward.5: Now go. …Drop in sometimes. Not often. …Well, often's fine. The cat will miss you. The cat, I said.
prokip.t.after.label: Beast speech
prokip.t.after.question: Grandad, the things the geese said!
prokip.after.0: Geese gossip, I told you. Never trust a goose. A cow you can trust. A cow doesn't lie, she can't be bothered.
prokip.t.vesna.label: And Vesna?
prokip.t.vesna.question: Why don't you go and see her yourself?
prokip.vesna.0: Myself? Over the river? At my age? …She'd say I'd come to admit it rained.
prokip.vesna.1: And maybe it did rain. But admitting it, that's going too far. Go on, go.
prokip.vesna.t.who.label: Did Prokip
prokip.vesna.t.who.question: Who's Did Prokip?
prokip.vesna.who.0: A vorozhbyt. Lives in the forest past the chumak bridge, to the east, further than decent people go.
prokip.vesna.who.1: Cross as a wasp in a jug. I learned from him once, so I'd know. If you see him, tell him he's an old fool. He knows.
prokip.vesna.t.msg.label: Regards from Prokip
prokip.vesna.t.msg.question: Did Prokip sends his regards. And asks whether it'll rain on Kupala.
prokip.vesna.msg.1: RAIN?! All these years he won't admit it, and now he MOCKS me?!
prokip.vesna.msg.2: And you, the messenger! Out of my sight! Out, I said, before I see you off with the broom!
prokip.odarka.t.nights.label: The nights
prokip.odarka.t.nights.question: How are you sleeping, Odarka?
prokip.odarka.nights.0: You won't believe it, kobzar. He comes. My Stepan. Every night. He stands on the threshold and says nothing.
prokip.odarka.nights.1: I sleep so well. Only I'm cold somehow. And my hands won't mind me. Pour you one? Oh, I've spilled it…
prokip.odarka.t.after.label: That night
prokip.odarka.t.after.question: How are you, Odarka?
prokip.odarka.after.0: I knew it wasn't him. Stepan never went without his hat. Not even to me.
prokip.odarka.after.1: Seven years I didn't lock the door. Now I'll lock it. And cry, the way people cry. And then I'll open it again, because it's a korchma.
prokip.odarka.after.2: Sit down. Tonight it's on the house. Just don't tell Okhrim.
prokip.well.0: You lower the sieve into the well. It comes up full, for one moment.
prokip.well.1: The water trickles through the holes straight into your boots. The well's crane creaks. It seems to be laughing.
prokip.well.toast: The sieve is empty. Your boots are not. Go back to Did Prokip.
ui.promptLabel.sieve: Fill the sieve at the well
perelesnyk.scene.0: Over the korchma, a streak of fire. It falls onto the threshold and becomes a man. Tall. Bareheaded. No shadow.
perelesnyk.scene.1: Odarka stands in the doorway in her feast-day kerchief. She smiles the way she hasn't smiled in seven years.
perelesnyk.scene.2: "Stepan… you came," she whispers. He says nothing. He smells of burning. In your pocket: Prokip's poppy seed.
perelesnyk.driven.0: The poppy falls on the threshold and the fire shies as if from boiling water. You take up the kobza and sing.
perelesnyk.driven.1: What was Stepan crackles, writhes, and scatters in sparks over the road. The horse at the korchma lets out a long breath.
perelesnyk.driven.2: Odarka sits down on the threshold. She doesn't scream. She just cries, quietly, the way widows cry.
perelesnyk.spared.0: You step back into the dark. The korchma door closes. In the window, two people, and only one shadow.
perelesnyk.spared.1: In the morning Odarka will be happy. And a little paler than yesterday.
perelesnyk.toast.driven: The perelesnyk is driven off. Go back to Did Prokip.
perelesnyk.toast.spared: You left Odarka her night. The perelesnyk will come again tomorrow.
animal.dog.name: The dog
animal.dog.0: The otaman ate salo by himself again. I saw. I see everything. Nobody asks me.
animal.dog.1: The Chort by the millstone smells of sulphur and perfume. Bark at him? No. I'm not stupid.
animal.dog.2: You smell of fish. You're good. No, really, you're good. Scratch here.
animal.dog.3: At night Solokha flies out of the mill on a broom. I bark. They tell me "quiet". Then they wonder.
animal.dog.night: Hrr… a bone… a big bone… hrr… don't touch it…
animal.goose.name: A goose
animal.goose.0: Honk. We saw Radek hiding chervintsi in the anvil. Tell no one. Honk.
animal.goose.1: This pond is ours. The Bolotianyk, off in his bog over the river, thinks all water is his. Let him think. Honk-honk-honk.
animal.goose.2: Don't come closer. …Fine, come closer. Got bread? No? Then go.
animal.goose.3: Every morning Vesna talks to the herbs. The herbs answer her. We heard. We hear everything. Honk.
animal.goose.night: Shhh. Head under the wing. We're sleeping. You sleep too.
animal.cow.name: The cow
animal.cow.0: Moo… Grass. Grass again. Have you ever thought about grass? I do. All the time.
animal.cow.1: The windmill turns. Solokha sleeps in the flour by day. Someone has to know. Now you do. Moo.
animal.cow.2: My name is Krasulya. You didn't ask. Nobody asks. Thank you for listening.
animal.cow.3: Did Prokip once treated my udder. Grumbled all day. Good old man. Moo-oo.
animal.cow.night: Moo… sleeping… cows sleep too, son… moo…
animal.horse.name: The horse
animal.horse.0: Okhrim says I'm a Cossack horse. I've hauled firewood all my life. But it's nice.
animal.horse.1: Give me an apple. None? People… You've got a kobza, and no apple.
animal.horse.2: The chumaky say the salt in the Crimea is white as snow. I don't like snow. Or chumaky.
animal.horse.fire: Fire over the korchma again. Every night. The shynkarka comes out onto the threshold and smiles. Horses see such things. Horses are afraid.
animal.horse.calm: The fire doesn't fly any more. The shynkarka cries, but she eats. If a person eats, she'll live.
quest.prokip.title: Did Prokip
quest.prokip.find: Vesna says a vorozhbyt lives in the forest past the chumak bridge, to the east. Find him.
quest.prokip.sieve: Bring Did Prokip water from the well in the khutir. In a sieve.
quest.prokip.sieveBack: The water ran out. Go back to Did Prokip.
quest.prokip.message: Give Vesna Did Prokip's regards and ask whether it'll rain on Kupala.
quest.prokip.answer: Vesna chased you out with a broom. Tell Did Prokip.
quest.prokip.perelesnyk: At night by the korchma: the perelesnyk. Poppy on the threshold, and sing.
quest.prokip.reward: The perelesnyk is gone. Go back to Did Prokip.
quest.prokip.done: You understand the beasts. Listen to the dog, the geese, the cow and the horse.
char.onufriy.name: Onufriy
char.onufriy.role: Hermit · keeps a candle in the cave
char.omelko.name: Omelko
char.omelko.role: Blind kobzar · sees fine in the dark
char.zmiy.name: Zmiy
char.zmiy.role: The old serpent · lies on a dowry
char.vohnyk.name: Vohnyk
char.sydir.name: Sydir
cave.onufriy.intro: Softly, son. Everything carries in here, footsteps and thoughts alike. I'm Onufriy. I used to be a monk; now I only mind a candle. Sit, warm yourself.
cave.onufriy.again: The candle still burns. Ask what you like.
cave.onufriy.t.who.label: About the hermit
cave.onufriy.t.who.question: What are you doing in a cave, father?
cave.onufriy.who.0: I ran from an abbot who loved money more than God. A cave doesn't ask who you are.
cave.onufriy.who.1: I live on the bowls of kulish good people bring, and on a quiet nobody brings.
cave.onufriy.t.candle.label: About the candle
cave.onufriy.t.candle.question: What is the candle for?
cave.onufriy.candle.0: So the old serpent in the deep knows someone is here and means no harm. He hasn't eaten anyone in ages, but who can tell.
cave.onufriy.candle.1: And so there's somewhere to come back to from the dark. A candle is like a hut: you know it's there.
cave.onufriy.t.zmiy.label: About the serpent
cave.onufriy.t.zmiy.question: What is that serpent in the deep?
cave.onufriy.zmiy.0: The Zmiy. Old, very old and very sad. Once he carried off a girl, Maryna of Verbivka. She never loved him, and she wasted away here.
cave.onufriy.zmiy.1: You won't take him by force. But he listens to a song. A sad one, son, only a sad one.
cave.onufriy.zmiy.lulled.0: Hear that? Not snoring, sighing. It's long since I heard him sleep like this.
cave.onufriy.zmiy.lulled.1: You've done more than I have, kobzar. For twenty years I only prayed for him.
cave.onufriy.t.omelko.label: About the blind man
cave.onufriy.t.omelko.question: Who is the old man with the kobza in the corner?
cave.onufriy.omelko.0: Omelko. He came here blind and I could see. Now I think he sees more than I do.
cave.onufriy.omelko.1: Go and hear him out. A kobzar never turns away a kobzar.
cave.onufriy.t.tunnel.label: About the draught
cave.onufriy.t.tunnel.question: Why does the flame lean toward the back?
cave.onufriy.tunnel.0: See? Behind where the serpent lies there's a crack in the back wall. It draws like a cellar. An old way, from the grandfathers.
cave.onufriy.tunnel.1: But while he's awake you won't get past him. Without knowing it, he guards that way.
cave.onufriy.tunnel.open.0: You went through? Then you know: the tunnel runs under the river to the kaplytsia. Grandfathers' work, hiding from the Tatars.
cave.onufriy.tunnel.open.1: Just don't tell me what's in it. I'm a monk; better I don't know what is worth stealing there.
cave.omelko.intro: Who's there? Don't say; I hear it in the step: a lad, kobza on his back, a small sin to carry. I'm Omelko. Sit, brother.
cave.omelko.again: Ah, it's you. The kobza's there; I heard a string creak. Ask.
cave.omelko.t.who.label: About the blind kobzar
cave.omelko.t.who.question: Who are you, grandfather?
cave.omelko.who.0: Walked the fairs forty years. Sang while there was a mug, and drank while there was a song.
cave.omelko.who.1: Then I went blind. People say from smoke. I say from seeing too much.
cave.omelko.t.eyes.label: About the dark
cave.omelko.t.eyes.question: How do you live here without light?
cave.omelko.eyes.0: Day or night, it's all one to me. It's you who can see that fear the dark; to me it's just a house.
cave.omelko.eyes.1: I hear where the bats are. I hear where the water is. The old serpent I hear best of all: he breathes like a very tired cow.
cave.omelko.t.marusia.label: Teach me a duma
cave.omelko.t.marusia.question: Will you teach me a duma?
cave.omelko.marusia.0: There's one. “Marusia Bohuslavka,” about a girl who in captivity forgot neither her faith nor her people, and led the captives to freedom. Listen.
cave.omelko.marusia.1: Omelko sings low and slow, and you catch every note. Now the duma is in your fingers. It is sad, as it should be. Sing it when someone's heart is heavy.
cave.omelko.t.singAgain.label: About the duma
cave.omelko.t.singAgain.question: How is “Marusia” best sung?
cave.omelko.singAgain.0: Slowly. Don't hurry it: a duma is not a hopak, it has nowhere to be.
cave.omelko.singAgain.1: And sing to the serpent with no frills. A hundred years he heard flattery; he knows the truth from the first note.
cave.omelko.singAgain.lulled: Hear the quiet? That's him asleep. Even stone sighs at a duma like that.
cave.omelko.t.zmiy.label: About the Zmiy
cave.omelko.t.zmiy.question: Why does the Zmiy only like sad songs?
cave.omelko.zmiy.0: What would you want, if you'd lost the only one? Merry songs are salt on a wound to him.
cave.omelko.zmiy.1: Sing a merry one, and you wake and anger him. An ordinary one, he listens and doesn't stir. A sad one, and he sleeps. Simple, like everything true.
cave.omelko.t.kobza.label: About the kobza
cave.omelko.t.kobza.question: Where did you get your kobza?
cave.omelko.kobza.0: My brother-in-song left it to me when he died. The wood still remembers his hands.
cave.omelko.kobza.1: Yours is the same: a sister to mine. Just see you don't hit people with it. Unless they've earned it.
cave.zmiy.intro: Who's this? Smells of smoke, road and youth. I am the Zmiy. Don't be afraid; I haven't eaten anyone in a hundred years. You're not tasty.
cave.zmiy.again: You again. Make it short; I'm old and tired.
cave.zmiy.t.who.label: About the serpent
cave.zmiy.t.who.question: Who are you?
cave.zmiy.who.0: I was a fiery serpent. I flew over the Dnipro and the girls hid behind their huts. I enjoyed it.
cave.zmiy.who.1: Now I lie. My wings wore away on the stone long ago. Old age is when even flying is too much trouble.
cave.zmiy.t.bride.label: About the dowry's owner
cave.zmiy.t.bride.question: Whose dowry is it?
cave.zmiy.bride.0: Maryna's. From Verbivka. She was walking with her buckets, I saw her and thought that to love was to want to have.
cave.zmiy.bride.1: I brought her here. Three springs she said nothing. I brought her gold, flowers, stars from the sky, and she looked through me.
cave.zmiy.bride.2: On the fourth she did not wake. I can't eat without her, or sleep. I lie on her dowry, and that's all.
cave.zmiy.t.hoard.label: About the gold
cave.zmiy.t.hoard.question: What is the gold under you?
cave.zmiy.hoard.0: A dowry. A kerchief of chervintsi that a girl's father tied. Not mine. I never touched it. I lie on it as on a palm.
cave.zmiy.hoard.1: Whoever touches them while I'm awake will regret it. But when I sleep… well, a dream is no watchman.
cave.zmiy.t.sing.label: About a song
cave.zmiy.t.sing.question: What would you like to hear?
cave.zmiy.sing.0: Sing me something true. Not about wine, not a hopak. I've watched enough of other people's laughter, and it frightens me.
cave.zmiy.sing.1: Play how bitter it is for you, kobzar. And maybe I'll sleep for the first time in a whole life.
cave.zmiy.sleepIntro: The Zmiy sleeps, nose in the dowry. Through his sleep he mutters: “Maryna…”
cave.zmiy.t.dream.label: Listen
cave.zmiy.t.dream.question: What are you muttering, old one?
cave.zmiy.dream.0: “…went off with the buckets… laughing… didn't look back…”
cave.zmiy.dream.1: He claws at the air, then goes quiet. You pity him, but it is good that he can sleep.
cave.zmiy.t.hoardSleep.label: About the kerchief
cave.zmiy.t.hoardSleep.question: What is under his tail?
cave.zmiy.hoardSleep.0: Under his tail, in an embroidered kerchief, lie chervintsi: a dowry no one will carry home. You could take it; he sleeps.
cave.zmiy.hoardSleep.1: A conscience is like a kerchief: thin, yet it holds. Decide for yourself.
cave.zmiy.hoardTaken: The kerchief under his tail is empty. The Zmiy sighs in his sleep and doesn't wake.
cave.vohnyk.intro: Oh! Someone's glowing! No, not you, me. I'm bright. I'm somebody. I'm Vohnyk… I think. Or Vohon. Or Ohnyk.
cave.vohnyk.again: Oh, you! Do we know each other? I forgot. Do you glow too? No? Pity.
cave.vohnyk.t.who.label: About the flame
cave.vohnyk.t.who.question: How did you get here?
cave.vohnyk.who.0: I wandered the marsh, then the forest, then wandered into the cave. It's warm here and nobody asks me to lead them home.
cave.vohnyk.who.1: I used to lead people. I don't remember where. I think they don't either.
cave.vohnyk.t.name.label: About his name
cave.vohnyk.t.name.question: What's your name?
cave.vohnyk.name.0: Vohnyk! Or… wait. No, Vohnyk. Definitely. Unless not.
cave.vohnyk.name.1: Yesterday I knew. Today I know that I knew yesterday. That's nearly the same.
cave.vohnyk.t.pool.label: About the pool
cave.vohnyk.t.pool.question: What is glowing in the pool?
cave.vohnyk.pool.0: That's me! No, it's it. No, both of us. Look: it flickered, I flickered. We're talking.
cave.vohnyk.pool.1: It says nothing, but it listens. It understands me better than people do.
cave.vohnyk.t.lure.label: About the marsh
cave.vohnyk.t.lure.question: Did you really lead people into the bog?
cave.vohnyk.lure.0: Me?! Never. I only shone. They walked. Where they walked was none of my business.
cave.vohnyk.lure.1: Now I'm just a speck of light in a cave. Nobody follows me. I even like it. I don't remember why.
cave.sydir.intro: Sh! Quieter, lad… Ah, a kobza. One of ours. I'm Sydir, a chumak. Was. Now I'm the one who carries salt past other men's tollgates. Sit, the lamp is for two.
cave.sydir.again: Oh, one of ours. Want to learn something, or just to hear me grumble?
cave.sydir.t.who.label: About Sydir
cave.sydir.t.who.question: What are you doing down here?
cave.sydir.who.0: Hauled salt from Crimea forty years. The tolls at the tollgates are such that the oxen would sooner sell themselves.
cave.sydir.who.1: So I found a way round, underground. No tollgate sees it, none takes its cut.
cave.sydir.t.tunnel.label: About the tunnel
cave.sydir.t.tunnel.question: Who dug this tunnel?
cave.sydir.tunnel.0: The first people of Zalissya. When the Tatars came raiding, they hid children and grain underground. Dug it three winters.
cave.sydir.tunnel.1: One end is in the cave, behind the old serpent. The other under the kaplytsia. Where else to hide but under God?
cave.sydir.tunnel.2: I only cleared it and hung the lamps. They say it was once longer, all the way to the Sich. But beyond here it caved in.
cave.sydir.t.bones.label: About the bones
cave.sydir.t.bones.question: Whose bones are those by the wall?
cave.sydir.bones.0: A sentry's. He stood here while the Tatars poked about above. Whether his own people came for him, I don't know.
cave.sydir.bones.1: His purse lies beside him. My conscience wouldn't let me. Maybe yours will.
cave.sydir.t.goods.label: About the goods
cave.sydir.t.goods.question: What are you hiding here?
cave.sydir.goods.0: Salt, tobacco, a little tar, a cask of horilka. All honest but the road.
cave.sydir.goods.1: I'd sell you some, but who pays a kobzar? Sleep easy: what you don't have can't be stolen.
cave.sydir.t.song.label: A song for the road
cave.sydir.t.song.question: Do you know a song for the road?
cave.sydir.song.0: I do. “Oh, don't go, Hrytsiu,” about a lad whom the evening gatherings will bring to no good. Merry, though it's about trouble.
cave.sydir.song.1: Sydir mutters it in a hoarse bass, and the lamp seems to wink. Now it's yours. Play it when you want laughter.
cave.rumor.myroslav.label: About a cave
cave.rumor.myroslav.question: Is there a cave anywhere near?
cave.rumor.myroslav.0: Across the river, south of the old oak, there's a hill of stone. The children say a Zmiy sleeps in it. And the children are probably right.
cave.rumor.myroslav.1: I never went; I'm too old for foolishness. But a monk lives there, keeping a candle. He's alive and well, so the Zmiy can't be raging. Careful with the kobza: he likes only sad songs.
cave.rumor.okhrim.label: About a way underground
cave.rumor.okhrim.question: I heard someone dug under the river. True?
cave.rumor.okhrim.0: True, son. My grandfather said that when the Tatars came, the first Zalissya folk dug a way from the cave to under the kaplytsia. There's a hatch under the rug by the analoy.
cave.rumor.okhrim.1: Nobody's gone down in ages. But they say a lamp burns there. Likely someone's trading past the toll. I'll tell nobody; I'm no saint myself.
ui.play.audience.marusia: “Marusia Bohuslavka.” The duma pours out slowly, like a river in bondage. Nobody laughs. Vesna turns away; the otaman stares into the fire.
ui.play.audience.hrytsiu: “Oh, don't go, Hrytsiu.” First everyone laughs, then they join in, and Radek is already thumping his mug on the bench and winking at the girls.
ui.enterHut.zmiieva: The Serpent's Cave. Dark, cool, smelling of wet stone. Somewhere water drips, and somewhere something large is breathing.
ui.enterHut.lazna: The tunnel. A narrow way under the river. Candles in niches in the walls, and far ahead a lamp flickers.
cave.sing.lulled.toast: {song}: the Zmiy listens and falls asleep. His coils draw back, leaving a crack in the back wall.
cave.sing.lulled.0: …Maryna… No. It isn't her, it's a song. Thank you, kobzar.
cave.sing.lulled.1: I'll sleep. You do what you must. Only know: it is her dowry, not mine and not yours.
cave.sing.listens.toast: {song}: the Zmiy opens one eye, listens, and does not stir. This is not what he is waiting for.
cave.sing.listens.0: Pretty. But I've heard that before. A hundred times.
cave.sing.listens.1: Not about me. Play something that hurts.
cave.sing.wakes.toast: {song}: the Zmiy jerks awake! His head snaps up, and the bats burst from the ceiling.
cave.sing.wakes.0: SILENCE! Who dares make merry in my cave?!
cave.sing.wakes.1: Forgive me, kobzar. I am angry not at you but at gladness. Try another.
cave.toast.caveHeard: Now you know where the Serpent's Cave is: across the river, south of the old oak.
cave.toast.lazKnown: In the kaplytsia there is a hatch under the rug. A tunnel runs underground all the way to the cave.
cave.toast.hoard: You carefully slide the kerchief of chervintsi out from under his tail. Chervintsi: +{n}.
cave.toast.pouch: A few chervintsi are left in the sentry's purse. Chervintsi: +{n}.
cave.prompt.tunnelEast: Climb the ladder to the kaplytsia ⬆
cave.pass.crackFirst: You squeeze into the crack in the back wall. Tight and cold, the earth smells of damp, and far ahead a lamp flickers.
cave.pass.tunnelWest: You climb up to the cave.
cave.pass.tunnelWestFirst: You climb out into the cave, into the Zmiy's lair, behind his coils.
cave.pass.tunnelEastFirst: You climb the ladder and push at the hatch, and above you it smells of wax and incense: the Zalissya kaplytsia.
cave.pass.chapelHatchFirst: You fold back the rug, and under it is a hatch with an iron ring. A ladder leads down into the dark, where a light flickers.
pond.bathe.fresh: Coat on the bank, yourself in the water. Warm on top, icy by the bottom. The road's dust washes off: until morning you are fresh as a cucumber. CHA +1
pond.bathe.again: Back in the water. The karas swim off, offended.
pond.bathe.night: The night water is black and warm. They say drowned maidens swim here on May nights. Something brushes your leg. Lily stems. Probably.
pond.shore: You climb out onto the bank, shake yourself like a dog and pull your coat on over the wet.
prokip.vesna.angry.0: You?! And you dare show your face! Out!
prokip.vesna.angry.1: I don't talk to old fools' messengers. Out.
prokip.vesna.angry.2: The broom is right here, singer. Don't test me.
prokip.vesna.t.sorry.label: Apologize
prokip.vesna.t.sorry.question: Vesna, I'm sorry. I didn't know what that question meant.
prokip.vesna.sorry.0: Didn't know. …Of course you didn't. That's what he was counting on, the old fox.
prokip.vesna.sorry.1: It's not your fault. You're just a fool sent by another fool. An older one.
prokip.vesna.sorry.2: Sit down. Mint tea? …And so you know: it DID rain. Tell him that. No, don't tell him anything.
prokip.vesna.toast.chased: Vesna chases you out with a broom. Accurately.
quest.vesnaSorry.title: Vesna is cross
quest.vesnaSorry.why: Vesna chased you out with a broom. Did Prokip knows why.
quest.vesnaSorry.done: Vesna has forgiven you. And it did rain.
